sentences.text: Qijianglong was a herbivorous sauropod dinosaur belonging to the family Mamenchisauridae.

The holotype specimen, QJGPM 1001, is a partial skeleton containing the rear skull, partial lower jaw, seventeen neck vertebrae, six back vertebrae, ribs, tail vertebrae, a pubic bone, and foot bones. This individual likely represents a large but immature juvenile.
The holotype of Qijianglong was approximately fifteen meters long and possessed a long neck.
A unique feature of Qijianglong is that the processus basipterygoideus on the lower braincase is plate-like and oriented along the body axis.
Qijianglong neck vertebrae had finger-shaped extensions on the joint processes that stiffened the neck horizontally while allowing vertical movement.
The rear neck vertebrae of Qijianglong featured pneumatic openings located between the rib joint process and the neural spine.
The pubic bone of Qijianglong had a strongly concave front edge that directed its lower end forward rather than downward.
A single vertebra of Qijianglong was first found in the early 1990s by a farmer in his backyard in Sichuan, China.
A rich fossil quarry was uncovered in 2006 at a construction site in the Qijiang District.
The species Qijianglong guokr was named and described in 2015 by a team of eight researchers including Xing Lida and Philip John Currie.

Qijianglong is classified within the family Mamenchisauridae in a basal position, just above Omeisaurus tianfuensis on the evolutionary tree. The parent group for the genus Qijianglong is the family Mamenchisauridae.
Fossils of Qijianglong have been found in the Suining Formation in China.

The age of the Suining Formation where Qijianglong was found is debated, with estimates ranging from the Late Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous. However, radiometric dating suggests the Suining Formation containing the holotype dates to the late Aptian of the Middle Cretaceous, rather than the Late Jurassic. Qijianglong lived during the Middle Cretaceous, approximately 115 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
